plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial with large, lush, often fragrant double or single flowers atop sturdy stems with deeply lobed green foliage. It is one of the most beloved cottage garden plants and a popular cut flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to China and Siberia; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America, Europe, and Asia
plants.funFact: Peonies can live and bloom for over 100 years, and ants are often seen on the buds feeding on nectar, though they are not required for blooming.

plants.name: Rosa gallica
plants.description: A hardy, deciduous shrub with fragrant, semi-double flowers that have golden stamens at the center. It is one of the oldest cultivated roses and a parent to many modern garden roses.
plants.location: Native to southern and central Europe and western Asia; grown in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Rosa gallica 'Officinalis', the Apothecary's Rose, was used medicinally in the Middle Ages and its petals retain fragrance when dried.

plants.name: Leucanthemum vulgare
plants.description: A hardy wildflower forming clumps of upright stems topped with white petals radiating around a bright yellow center. It thrives in meadows, roadsides, and disturbed grasslands.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer (May to August)
plants.location: Native to Europe and temperate Asia; naturalized across North America, Australia, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: Oxeye daisy flower heads track the sun, and in some regions it is known as the 'Moon Daisy' because the white petals stand out at dusk.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall, graceful tree with fern-like leaves that is covered in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In the Northern Hemisphere subtropics it blooms in late spring and early summer, carpeting streets with fallen petals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in California, Mexico, Florida, the Mediterranean, and southern Africa
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, the city is known as the 'Jacaranda City' due to its tens of thousands of jacaranda trees, and a local superstition says a falling bloom on your head brings good luck.
